newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers bullish on US debt--MCM survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers bullish on US debt--MCM survey.

text.p: U.S. money managers remained bullish on their debt portfolios over the past week, pushing the 10-plus year duration sector to its highest level since last August, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.

In the week ending July 21, 40 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 32 percent in the previous week. Seven percent underweighted it, while the remaining 53 percent were "neutral."
"The 10-plus years is the highest level since last August," said MCM MoneyWatch economist Astrid Adolfson, who conducts the weekly survey.
In addition, "Cash levels rose ... as profits were taken in the short end," she said.
Cash as a percentage of assets rose to 3.25 percent from 3.09 percent registered the previous week.
Durations as a percentage of benchmark remained steady at 108.1 percent, the same as the previous two weeks.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 38 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," higher than 29 percent in the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" dropped to 12 percent from 15 percent the previous week.
Fifty percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 44 percent the prior week.
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 40 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 20 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
